Nullus Engine/Real-time rendering

RENDERING / FRAMEGRAPH / RHI

Real-time 3D rendering from scene to GPU

Nullus connects scene updates, FrameGraph, and an explicit RHI in a traceable rendering pipeline shared by the Editor and Player.

The path from scene to screen

The Game Thread updates scene rendering data through commands, the Render Thread builds the frame, and the RHI lane translates and submits native commands. SceneRenderStore holds persistent rendering data, while each frame carries camera, view, and output parameters.

Game Thread→Render Thread→RHI Submit

Rendering work uses TaskGraph execution lanes. GPU fences control frame-resource reuse, keeping thread, resource, and submission responsibilities clear when profiling or extending the engine.

FrameGraph manages rendering passes

FrameGraph describes each pass's inputs, outputs, and resource states, then manages pass dependencies and resource transitions. Both the forward and deferred paths share this resource management model.

  • Forward includes a depth prepass, forward shading, transparent objects, skybox, and editor overlays.
  • Deferred includes the GBuffer, clustered lighting, decals, deferred lighting, and transparent output.
  • Large-scene foundations include visibility collection, draw-command caching, instancing, and static-mesh LOD.

HLSL, ShaderLab, and PBR materials

HLSL is the engine's maintained shader source. Compilation produces DXIL, SPIR-V, and reflection data. ShaderLab describes material properties and rendering state, while the built-in StandardPBR provides a baseline for imported models.

The Material Editor supports material parameters, ShaderLab, and ShaderGraph with previews. Model import can produce meshes, materials, textures, and Prefab sub-assets.

Graphics backends and platform status

Windows uses DX12 and Linux or WSL uses Vulkan 1.1, both current runtime mainlines. macOS has a Metal build target and native backend, with device runtime validation tracked separately. DX12 HZB occlusion is enabled according to device capabilities.

For feature availability and validation scope, see graphics backends and large scenes and the platform matrix.
